title: There Is a State Unknown, Unseen
description: There Is a State Unknown, Unseen in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Jane Taylor wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 357, “The Unseen World”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: There is a state un-known, un-seen, Where par-ted souls must be; And but a step doth lie be-tween That world of souls and me.

lines: There is a state unknown, unseen,
And but a step doth lie between
That world of souls and me.
I see no light, I hear no sound,
Yet angels pitch their tents around,
The things unseen, O God, reveal;
Till I shall feel, and see, and know,
That those I love are near.
Impart the faith that soars on high,
That holds sweet converse with the sky,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Jane Taylor died in 1824.
credits: Words by Jane Taylor (1783–1824), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
